scope: Talvora Memory Phase 4: local CPU-first hybrid retrieval keeps FTS5 as deterministic fallback and adds a benchmark-selected multilingual ONNX embedding provider, revisioned float32 vectors in SQLite, bounded managed cosine search, stale-vector exclusion, and resumable re-embedding.

libraries.verified: Current SQLite guidance supports additive durable metadata tables, foreign-key cascade cleanup, CHECK constraints, BLOB storage, and bounded indexed queries. Talvora Memory Phase 4 stores normalized float32 embeddings as length-constrained BLOBs with model id/revision, content hash, and canonical item update timestamp while retaining FTS5 as the authoritative deterministic fallback.

Current ASP.NET Core MCP filter contract: ordinary AddCallToolFilter filters wrap CallTool exactly once around the downstream handler, can resolve services from request.Services, and must preserve returned CallToolResult/exception semantics. Returned failures may use IsError=true or structured result state rather than exceptions. Talvora Phase 3 therefore classifies success/failure after the downstream call, records only safe metadata, and catches all learning-side failures so observation can never alter, mask, cancel, or replace the underlying tool result.

Current Microsoft Windows/PowerShell task guidance supports manual task execution and explicit enable/disable control. Talvora uses that lifecycle for the opt-in Penpot task: disabled while idle, explicitly enabled before Start-ScheduledTask, and stopped/disabled again when the on-demand MCP is not in use.

Current Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers guidance confirms SentencePieceTokenizer/Create and EncodeToIds support. Talvora Phase 4 validated Microsoft SentencePiece tokenization against the Hugging Face XLM-R tokenizer using the explicit XLM-R id remap, then reproduced the benchmark ranking with Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers 2.0.0 plus Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime 1.30.0.

Current WPF-UI Snackbar guidance confirms presenter-owned nonmodal notification UX with explicit timeout; Talvora keeps the existing WPF-UI design language while using a tray-owned WPF progress card so full text, coalescing, hover pause and lifecycle remain under Talvora control.

Current WPF dispatcher guidance confirms UI callbacks execute through Dispatcher operations and recommends moving blocking work away from the dispatcher before marshaling results back to UI state. Talvora keeps the cross-process Mutex acquire/release wholly on one worker thread, performs bounded event-history and raw-log file reads through async worker boundaries, parallelizes independent detail health/version/event work, and uses a nonblocking gate plus selected-MCP identity check to prevent overlapping or stale live-log refreshes.
